title: Granular consumption windows and entitlement inheritance for hybrid plans (hourly smoothing, project-level caps, and offline reconciliation)
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for introducing two linked features in Pricing & Billing v3: 1) configurable consumption smoothing windows (hourly and sub-hourly) to reduce noisy burst-related overages while preserving latency-sensitive quotas, and 2) entitlement inheritance and override rules across workspace -> project -> route levels to express real customer billing constructs. The goal is to reduce false-positive overage charges, provide predictable developer-facing quotas, and enable accurate offline reconciliation for invoices.

Background & motivation:
- Customers using Dedicated and Private deployments have complained about spiky traffic creating surprise overages during short bursts (e.g., 30–90s) even though monthly consumption is within plan.
- Platform teams want ability to set project-level caps distinct from workspace defaults and to support route-level hard limits for high-cost endpoints.
- Current metering is strictly per-request-at-timestamp; there is no smoothing or sliding window aggregation, and there is no explicit inheritance model for entitlements. This causes billing disputes and manual credits.

Goals:
- Implement configurable smoothing windows (default 1 minute and 1 hour policies) that aggregate token usage for overage enforcement only; billing records remain per-request for audit but enforcement uses smoothed view when enabled.
- Introduce entitlement inheritance: workspace defaults -> project-level overrides -> route-level overrides with clear precedence and audit trail.
- Provide offline reconciliation tooling that can re-run enforcement logic with historical raw meter data to produce an adjusted invoice during dispute resolution.
- Minimize latency impact: smoothing must not increase request-response latency or affect runtime routing decisions.

Non-goals / Out of scope:
- Changing per-token price tiers (pricing change will be covered under separate PRD).
- Real-time chargebacks for Dedicated internal cost centers (accounting integration scope separate).

Stakeholders:
- PM: Miles Patel (assignee), Ava Chen (creator)
- Eng leads: Priya Raman (billing), Samir Khanna (runtime)
- Finance: Lydia Torres
- Solutions/SE: Nora Williams
- Legal & Compliance: Rajesh Iyer

Trade-offs & decisions to make:
- Smoothing window length: shorter windows reduce perceived fairness to bursty but latency-critical workloads, longer windows increase smoothing but may hide real overuse. We propose default windows 60s (burst smoothing) and 3600s (hour smoothing) and allow plan-level configuration.
- Enforcement vs billing record separation: we will keep raw meter records immutable and perform enforcement on derived smoothed aggregates; this preserves auditability and simplifies reconcilers.
- Entitlement precedence: explicit override model (route > project > workspace) with a transparent audit log surfaced in Console.

Implementation notes (high level):
- Metering pipeline: ingest per-request token counts into raw storage (unchanged). A separate aggregator service will compute sliding-window aggregates at configurable bucket sizes and expose them to the rate-limit/enforcement layer via a cache with TTL equal to bucket granularity.
- Enforcement: rate-limiter checks smoothed counters first (if enabled for the plan), then falls back to raw counters for billing-only calculations.
- Reconciliation: offline job replays raw meter events and applies the same smoothing/enforcement rules used at time-of-event to produce disputed invoice adjustments.

Audit & observability requirements:
- Console must show: effective entitlement for workspace/project/route, smoothing window applied, current smoothed consumption, raw token consumption, and time of last aggregation.
- Dashboards: percent of overages avoided by smoothing, number of invoices adjusted via offline reconciliation, disputed credit totals monthly.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind billing-aggregation-v2; internal pilot with 3 customers on Dedicated.
2) Add Console UI for entitlement overrides (read-only initially) and observability panels.
3) Allow admins to enable smoothing per plan; collect telemetry for 2 billing cycles.
4) Gradual rollout to all hosted plans once metrics validate reduction in false-positive overages and low incidence of chargebacks.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: smoothing hides actual abuse. Mitigation: keep raw records and surface both raw and smoothed counts; apply higher scrutiny (alerts) on activities where smoothed reduces enforcement but raw shows repeated high peaks.
- Risk: reconciliation job complexity. Mitigation: build incremental replay with checkpoints and synthetic test datasets; require sign-off from Finance before customer-facing credits.
requirements:
1) Functional:
- R1: Billing must support configuring per-plan smoothing windows (none, 60s, 300s, 3600s).
- R2: Enforcement layer must consult smoothed counters when smoothing is enabled for a plan; smoothed counters take precedence only for enforcement decisions (blocking/soft-throttle) not for final invoice line-item generation.
- R3: Entitlement model must support 3 levels (workspace, project, route) with explicit override and visibility.
- R4: Metering must continue to store raw per-request events immutable for at least 540 days.
- R5: Reconciliation job must be able to re-run enforcement logic for any invoice period and emit a delta file suitable for Finance ingestion.

2) UX/API:
- R6: Console UI to display effective entitlement and allow admins to set project and route overrides (initially behind feature flag as read-only for audit).
- R7: Public API must expose current smoothed consumption and raw consumption for a given project and route.

3) Observability & alerts:
- R8: Alert when smoothing reduces enforcement count by >50% for a plan over a 7-day window.
- R9: Billing telemetry must expose disputed invoice counts and credit amounts for Finance dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: When smoothing is disabled, enforcement behavior is unchanged from current baseline for all plans (regression test coverage).

AC2: For a plan with 60s smoothing enabled, simulated burst traffic (10x baseline for 45s) must not trigger an overage enforcement if the 60s smoothed token sum remains under plan cap, while raw meter still records the raw tokens (verified via logs).
AC3: Entitlement precedence is enforced: a route override set to a lower cap prevents a project or workspace cap from inheriting a higher effective limit (test vectors provided).

AC4: Reconciliation: given exported raw meter events for a disputed 30-day invoice, running the reconciliation job with historical smoothing config reproduces the enforcement decisions and produces a delta invoice file within 30 minutes for a typical 1M-event customer dataset.
AC5: Console displays both raw and smoothed consumption for workspace/project/route and shows which smoothing window was applied. UX review sign-off required from Design.
AC6: No measurable increase in p95 request latency attributable to smoothing checks on the enforcement path in production pilot (<= 2ms overhead), validated by tracing.
AC7: Finance accepts format of reconciliation delta file and signs off on automated minor credit (<$5000/month) issuance flow; larger credit issuance remains manual.
